title: Venesarvinen hirvi
description: The elk is a common image in many Finnish petroglyphs. A drawing of a bighorn elk based on the rock paintings of Astuvansalmi and Ruominkapia that resemble each other. The original images are partially worn; this drawing combines parts of both, and also includes my own imagination. These moose are called boat-horned, because their antlers resemble pictures of boats.
creator: Tuohirullan
period_label: Subneolithic / Combed Ware — Finnish Rock Paintings (Lahelma 2008)

title: Circuit Board for Rock Painting Versam-Safien 01
description: The artist refers to prehistoric rock paintings. These can be understood as precursors of Land Art. The drawing on this rock face represents an oversized computer board. This work thus encourages reflections on central switching points of our modern computer age in the light of prehistoric rock drawings.
creator: Analia Saban

title: Documenting petroglyphs
description: Documenting rock carvings by use of the so-called rubbing technique (Kalleby, Sweden). "The re-documentation of the rock carvings in Tanum was started in 1989 by Tanums Hällristningsmuseum Underslös and its supporting association, the Scandinavian Society for Prehistoric Art. It is carried out at the international working seminars arranged by the museum every summer, where a group consisting of somewhere between 25 and 30 volunteers from four or six different countries work for a week on the project of documenting the rock art of Tanum/ UNESCO World Heritage Area." For more information see: ww
